head: f80d776d9b431a057bc53089bcf6cdc80ed2fc1f
summary:
HF-026 is fixed as the design specified. tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:176-183 reads the rest of the line with '(?m)^harness: scratch kept at (.+?)\s*$'. It removes the folder only when the leaf is fsa-rules-* and the parent equals GetTempPath or $env:TEMP. harness.py:72 prints through stdout, so the ^ anchor holds under 2>&1 | Out-String. I re-ran tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 in both modes. All shapes (Space, TempNotTmp, Refused) exited 0, and so did -Shape Python against the real harness.py under the engine's python. Fitness check: all 61 rules hold. The test uses RuleCases' own Invoke-HarnessRaw, taken from its AST. It feeds a spaced TEMP and a TEMP that differs from TMP, and checks by Test-Path that the folder is gone, so the case really is exercised.

I then used the real harness.py to test two more TEMP shapes of the same local-account kind. The fixed guard still leaks the scratch copy in both:
- **8.3 short-form TEMP** (e.g. C:\Users\JOHNSM~1\..., which Windows often gives spaced or long account names): Python prints the short form. The diff runs GetFullPath on the TMP/TEMP side only, and [IO.Path]::GetFullPath expands ~ names, so the two sides never compare equal.
- **Non-ASCII account name**: harness.py's say() escapes the path to 'Jos\xe9', which matches neither side.

Both are minor, with the same consequence as HF-026. Both are reproduced, and one leaf-based change fixes both. There is no undeclared drift.

Second round: The second, adversarial pass over RuleCases.ps1:176-183 found nothing beyond round one's m1 (8.3 short-form TEMP) and m2 (non-ASCII TEMP escaped by harness.py's say()). Those two still stand as filed.

Checked this round, all without a new defect:
- **Regex '(?m)^harness: scratch kept at (.+?)\s*$'.**
  - A CRLF line ending works: the lazy `.+?` stops before `\r`, which `\s*` takes, and `$` matches before `\n`.
  - Trailing spaces and tabs are trimmed.
  - Only one line can match. harness.py prints 'scratch kept at' once, in its finally block (:734). Every other say() line is indented, or is a traceback whose source lines are indented, so the `^` anchor rules out a stray earlier match. That makes it stricter than the old unanchored pattern.
  - The path cannot be empty, because mkdtemp always returns a path.
- **Split-Path -Parent / -Leaf, run on real inputs.** Paths with `[1]`, with `*`, a drive root (C:\fsa-rules-x gives parent 'C:', and GetFullPath('C:\').TrimEnd('\') is also 'C:', so it matches) and a UNC share all split correctly and do not throw.
- **TEMP spelled differently.** A trailing backslash, doubled backslashes or forward slashes in TEMP are normalised the same way by Python's abspath (GetFullPathNameW) and by .NET GetFullPath. Duplicate entries in $temps are harmless, and a null $env:TEMP is filtered out.
- **Removal failures.** Remove-Item -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue can leave a partly removed folder when a handle is still open. That is unchanged from before the diff, and the builder measured no fsa-rules-* left after real C-006 and C-014 runs.
- **Removing the scratch copy even when a case did not expect the failure.** This also predates the diff and is outside HF-026.

findings.claim: The fixed guard normalises only one side of the comparison. $temps runs [IO.Path]::GetFullPath over GetTempPath() and $env:TEMP, and .NET's GetFullPath expands 8.3 short names (measured: GetFullPath('C:\PROGRA~1') = 'C:\Program Files'). $parent is the harness's own path, and Python's os.path.abspath keeps short names (measured: 'C:\PROGRA~1' stays 'C:\PROGRA~1'). So when %TEMP% is in 8.3 form, the scratch copy is still left behind, even though its parent is literally $env:TEMP. Windows commonly sets TEMP that way for long or spaced account names such as 'John Smith' (C:\Users\JOHNSM~1\...). That is the very account shape HF-026 is about. Reproduced with the real harness.py and RuleCases' own Invoke-HarnessRaw: TEMP=TMP='...\SL076-~1\LONGNA~1\AppData\Local\Temp' exited 2 and printed 'scratch kept at ...\LONGNA~1\...\fsa-rules-fut4re7t'. That folder was left behind. Without the GetFullPath on $env:TEMP, the raw TEMP value would have matched. The SL-076 test has no short-name shape.
findings.evidence: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:179 `$parent = (Split-Path -Parent $dir).TrimEnd('\')` compared with :180 `ForEach-Object { [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($_).TrimEnd('\') }`. eng/rules-harness/harness.py:716 tempfile.mkdtemp prints gettempdir()'s abspath, which is not expanded.
findings.fix: Normalise both sides the same way, with `$parent = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath((Split-Path -Parent $dir)).TrimEnd('\')`. Better, the leaf-based check in m2 also fixes m2. Add a ShortName shape to tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1: TEMP set to Scripting.FileSystemObject's .ShortPath of a spaced folder.

findings.claim: harness.py's say() prints every line as ASCII with backslashreplace. A %TEMP% under an account name with a non-ASCII letter (e.g. 'José Smith') is therefore printed as 'Jos\xe9 Smith'. The path Invoke-HarnessRaw reads back names a folder that does not exist. Its parent matches neither GetTempPath nor $env:TEMP, so the scratch copy of the repo is left in %TEMP%. This is the same leak HF-026 fixed for a space, now for another common local-account shape. Reproduced: TEMP=TMP='...\José Smith\Temp' printed 'scratch kept at ...\Jos\xe9 Smith\Temp\fsa-rules-reeuo6g2'. The real folder '...\José Smith\Temp\fsa-rules-reeuo6g2' was left behind.
findings.evidence: eng/rules-harness/harness.py:72 `print(text.encode("ascii", "backslashreplace").decode("ascii"), flush=True)`. tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:176-183 uses the escaped path as-is.
findings.fix: Take only the leaf from the line. mkdtemp's leaf is always ASCII: '(?m)^harness: scratch kept at .*[\\/](fsa-rules-[A-Za-z0-9_]+)\s*$'. Then, for each distinct folder in @(GetTempPath(), $env:TEMP), remove Join-Path <folder> <leaf> if it exists. This fixes m1 and m2 together, and it keeps the guard's rule that only a folder directly in TMP or TEMP is removed. Add a NonAscii shape to the SL-076 test.

obligations.evidence: tests/rules/RuleCases.ps1:176 now uses '(?m)^harness: scratch kept at (.+?)\s*$'. Lines 179-181 accept the folder only when the leaf is fsa-rules-* and the parent -ieq GetTempPath() or $env:TEMP. I re-ran tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1: the Space, TempNotTmp and Refused shapes exited 0, and -Shape Python against the real harness.py and the engine's venv python also exited 0. The spaced-TEMP and TEMP≠TMP shapes HF-026 names are removed. Adjacent shapes still leak; see m1 and m2.

cases.evidence: tests/bugs/SL-076-ScratchKeptPath.Tests.ps1 takes RuleCases.ps1's own Invoke-HarnessRaw from its AST (lines 38-41), not a copy. Shape-Space sets TMP=TEMP='...\Users\John Smith\AppData\Local\Temp'. Shape-TempNotTmp sets TMP=tmp-a and TEMP=tmp-b, and asserts that GetTempPath returned tmp-a. In both, a stand-in python.cmd makes %TEMP%\fsa-rules-sl076, prints the kept line and exits 2. Test-Removed asserts by Test-Path -LiteralPath that the folder is gone. Shape-Refused leaves three folders alone: one outside TMP/TEMP, one whose leaf is not fsa-rules-*, and a nested fsa-rules-*. Shape-Python runs the real harness.py with a spaced TEMP different from TMP. All of these ran green here. None of the shapes covers an 8.3 short-form TEMP or a non-ASCII one; see m1 and m2.

drift: Nothing departs from the design without being declared. The old guard accepted any fsa-rules-* folder anywhere below GetTempPath (StartsWith); the new one takes only a folder directly in TMP or TEMP. That narrowing follows the design's 'its parent is either GetTempPath or $env:TEMP', and the build declared it (the Refused shape). The fix is at RuleCases.ps1:176-183, not :170, because the new comment lines pushed it down.
As declared in the build's open list, the fix does not cover TMPDIR (which Python's gettempdir checks first). The same limit applies to the 8.3 and non-ASCII shapes filed as m1 and m2.
No new drift. The narrower guard (a folder only directly in TMP or TEMP, where the old one took any descendant of GetTempPath) follows the design and was declared by the build.
